paper_metadata.title: Derivative Pricing using Quantum Signal Processing

summary: The paper introduces a Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) method to encode derivative payoffs directly into amplitudes, eliminating costly quantum arithmetic. For pricing an autocallable with 3 assets and 20 timesteps, the approach reduces resources by ~16× in T-count and ~4× in logical qubits compared to prior arithmetic methods. The authors estimate that quantum advantage would require ~4.7k logical qubits, ~2.4×10^9 T gates, and a logical clock rate of ~45 MHz.

experiments.description: Resource-estimation experiment for pricing an autocallable derivative contract using QSP-based payoff evaluation, compared against the prior arithmetic/lookup-table reparameterization method.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation with QSP-based payoff encoding

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Log-returns are loaded into quantum registers via the reparameterization method; payoff conditions are evaluated on log-returns, and the final payoff is encoded into an ancilla amplitude using QSP. For the autocallable, binary payoff conditions are stored in k qubits and barrier condition in a b register; the final clause uses QSP on the final timestep return register.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expected payoff of an autocallable derivative contract by amplitude estimation on the payoff ancilla probability.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Binary payoff conditions and barrier conditions are computed with CNOT/Toffoli logic; the second payoff clause is conditionally encoded using QSP when the barrier condition is met and no earlier binary payoff has triggered.

problem_instance.description: Autocallable derivative contract with 3 assets and 20 timesteps; target approximation error 2e-3 and payoff encoding accuracy 1e-3.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic/market-parameterized stochastic log-return model under geometric Brownian motion; no explicit ticker/date dataset given.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Prepare independent standard normal registers N(0,1), transform to multivariate normal N(µ,Σ) for log-returns, then evaluate payoff conditions on log-returns; final timestep uses fixed-point representation with (n,p)=(15,5) and range R=25.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Resource estimation only; no empirical sampling runs reported. End-to-end resources estimated for Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation at confidence 1-α=0.68.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation for end-to-end resource estimation; classical comparison assumes 1 second pricing time from prior work
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical market-parameter selection for µ, Σ and payoff normalization; polynomial approximation generated via optimization-based Chebyshev method.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Amplitude estimation converts measured payoff probability to derivative price.

speedup_claims.conditions: via amplitude estimation for derivative pricing
speedup_claims.caveats: This is the standard QAE quadratic speedup claim; the paper is a resource-estimation study and does not run hardware experiments.

speedup_claims.conditions: autocallable contract benchmark with a=3 assets, T=20 timesteps, payoff accuracy 1e-3

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Quadratic speedup via amplitude estimation over Monte Carlo; end-to-end resource estimate given as 4.5×10^7 T-depth and 2.4×10^9 T-count for the benchmark instance.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo pricing baseline; no explicit asymptotic complexity stated in the paper text provided.
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: QSP with Usqrt reduces T-count by ~16x and logical qubits by ~4x versus arithmetic baseline; logical clock rate reduced by ~5x versus prior approach.
complexity_analysis.crossover_n: Not explicitly given; paper states quantum advantage requires 4.7k logical qubits and 10^9 T-gates at 45MHz.
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: 1 second assumed classical pricing time from prior work

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Autocallable derivative with 3 assets and 20 timesteps; advantage requires ~4.7k logical qubits and ~10^9 T-gates
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: ≈4.7k logical qubits, 2.4×10^9 T gates, logical clock rate ≈45 MHz
limiting_factors: Requires thousands of logical qubits with full error correction

notes: The paper is a resource-estimation study, not a hardware execution study; no real QPU or simulator backend is named.
